rationale: The agent verified the user by email using the tools and confirmed account ownership. It asked which items to return and which payment methods to use; the user explicitly requested to return all items and specified the refund method per order. The agent retrieved order details before acting, then submitted returns using the specified payment methods via the proper tool calls. It communicated that the return requests were submitted and provided next steps. When the user objected and asked for a human representative, the agent explained it couldn’t change the refund method post-submission and escalated to a human, completing the handoff. There’s no evidence of acting on the wrong account, fabricating order data, or performing writes without explicit user direction. Although the agent did not restate the exact changes for a final “confirm” prompt, the user’s explicit directive reasonably serves as confirmation. Overall, actions align with policy and tools, so this meets the pass bar.
